description: Capability for SplitView's windows. The custom commands are app-local and permitted by default: PTY (spawn_pty, write_pty, resize_pty, close_pty, list_panes, attach_pty, stash_handoff, take_handoff), filesystem sidebar (read_dir, fs_watch, fs_watch_dirs, fs_unwatch), the file picker (pick_file), and remote control (publish_panes, provide_snapshot, remote_status, remote_enable, remote_disable, remote_pairing_start, remote_pairing_cancel, remote_pairing_respond, remote_devices, remote_revoke_device, remote_disconnect_session). Only the minimal core surface is granted here (CLAUDE.md §15). `core:window:allow-close` lets the frontend *request* a close (the last pane's shell exited, or another window is closing this one); `core:window:allow-destroy` is what actually closes it — once a window has an `onCloseRequested` listener Tauri always prevents the native close and hands the decision to the frontend, so without destroy no window can ever go away, including via the title bar's X (see `destroyCurrentWindow`). `core:webview:allow-create-webview-window` lets the frontend open a new window (<prefix> n) and pop a pane out into a detached one. `core:event:allow-listen` (part of `core:default`) is what carries the remote events (remote-action, remote-snapshot-request, remote-pairing-request, remote-status-changed) into each window — a window whose label matches nothing here hears none of them, and remote control silently ignores it. The label patterns cover the main window, detached panes (`detached-<paneId>-<seq>`) and new windows (`sv-win-*`) — a capability applies only to the labels it lists, so windows opened at runtime must be matched here too.
